/-!
# Erdős Problem 163

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/163](https://www.erdosproblems.com/163)
- [BuEr75] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P., On the Ramsey number of graphs with small degree-ratio.
  Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai (1975).
- [Le17] Lee, C., Ramsey numbers of degenerate graphs. Ann. of Math. (2) 185 (2017), 791-829.
-/

namespace Erdos163

/--
The Burr-Erdős conjecture: For any $d\geq 1$ if $H$ is a graph such that every subgraph
contains a vertex of degree at most $d$ then
$$R(H)\ll_d n.$$

Solved by Lee [Le17], who proved that $R(H) \leq 2^{2^{O(d)}}n$.

This problem is #9 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_163 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d →
      ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (H : SimpleGraph V),
        H.IsDegenerate d →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey H : ℝ) ≤ C * Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos163

findings.description: The module reference [BuEr75] at lines 24–25 gives the incorrect title “On the Ramsey number of graphs with small degree-ratio.” The 1975 Burr–Erdős paper containing this conjecture is titled “On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs.” This is a bibliographic error; the theorem's mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The original paper's title page (p. 215) reads “ON THE MAGNITUDE OF GENERALIZED RAMSEY NUMBERS FOR GRAPHS,” by S. A. Burr and P. Erdős: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-26.pdf. The Erdős archive's entry 1975-26 and Lee's bibliography give the same title.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [BuEr75] title with “On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs.” The full publication reference is Infinite and finite sets, Vol. I, Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 10 (1975), 215–240.

reformulations.difference: The source defines degeneracy using all nonempty subgraphs, whereas H.IsDegenerate d tests nonempty finite vertex sets and counts neighbours in the corresponding induced subgraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any subgraph K, its vertex set induces a graph in H with at least all of K's edges. A vertex of induced degree at most d therefore has degree at most d in K. Conversely, induced subgraphs are subgraphs. Since V is finite, the Finset quantifier covers every vertex subset. In /workspace/review/subgraph_equivalence.lean I proved both the pointwise equivalence with literal H.Subgraph objects and the equivalence of the complete problem statements; I also checked that the neighbour-set cardinality equals the ordinary subgraph degree. These proofs do not depend on sorry.

reformulations.difference: The original Burr–Erdős formulation on p. 216 concerns bounded-arboricity families and includes off-diagonal Ramsey numbers R(G,H). The Lean theorem uses the standard diagonal, bounded-degeneracy formulation also stated explicitly in Lee's introduction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Arboricity a and degeneracy δ satisfy a ≤ δ ≤ 2a, with edgeless graphs harmless. Thus bounds uniform in either parameter translate to bounds uniform in the other. Given G and H of arboricity at most d, their disjoint union is 2d-degenerate and R(G,H) ≤ R(G ⊔ H), so the diagonal conjecture gives a constant times |V(G)|+|V(H)|. Conversely, apply the off-diagonal conjecture to (H,H), absorbing the factor 2. The original family formulation gives uniform constants by taking the family of all finite graphs of the prescribed bounded arboricity, up to isomorphism.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the Burr–Erdős conjecture. Its positive answer and research solved tag agree with Lee's result and the current Erdős database. The constant is correctly uniform over graphs once d is fixed. Ramsey containment is non-induced and injective; finite Ramsey theory rules out the sInf-of-empty default. Successful Lean tests in /workspace/review/scratch.lean include R(empty)=0, R(edgeless graph on n vertices)=n, and a triangle being 2-degenerate but not 1-degenerate. The erdosproblems.com/163 page remained inaccessible behind Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the mathematical claim was instead verified against both cited primary papers, with status additionally corroborated by the independent database.
